cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has been carrying the LORD's message to Jerusalem: wake up (Isaiah 52:1), and burst into songs of joy, for the LORD has comforted His people and redeemed Jerusalem (Isaiah 52:9). Now the message turns to someone called My Servant. The first thing it says is that this Servant will prosper.

cards.question: My Servant will prosper. True or false: He will also be lifted up and highly exalted.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: That's THREE ways to say UP in one sentence, friend: raised, lifted up and highly exalted. Then comes something hard: many were appalled at Him.

cards.question: Many were appalled at the Servant. What was His appearance like?

answers.text: Disfigured beyond that of any man
Bright like the face of an angel
Dressed like a king on his throne

cards.text: Then it flips: He will sprinkle many nations, and KINGS will shut their mouths because of Him. Kings, friend, the folks who give speeches for a living, sitting there with NOTHING to say.

cards.question: Why will kings shut their mouths because of the Servant?

answers.text: They will see what they were never told
They will lose a war against Israel
He will order them to keep quiet

cards.text: Then come two questions, back to back: "Who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?"

cards.question: True or false: the question "Who has believed our message?" sounds like everybody already believes it.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then comes a picture of the Servant growing up before Him like a tender shoot, like a root out of dry ground.

cards.question: The Servant grew up like a root out of dry ground. What is said about how He looked?

answers.text: Nothing in His looks drew people in
He looked like a king in a palace
Crowds came just to see His face

cards.text: "He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief." I think this one hurts, friend.

cards.question: The Servant was despised and rejected. He was treated like someone people hide their ___ from.

answers.text: faces
children
money

cards.text: Now here's the turn. He took up our infirmities, and He carried our sorrows.

cards.question: The Servant carried the sorrows of the people speaking. What did they think was happening to Him?

answers.text: That God had struck Him down
That He was hiding from God
That He was faking His pain

cards.text: And then comes the BUT. He was pierced for our transgressions, and He was crushed for our iniquities.

cards.question: The people speaking talk about a punishment that brought them peace. That punishment was upon the ___.

answers.text: Servant
nations
kings

cards.question: True or false: the people speaking say they are healed by the Servant's stripes.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: And here's the honest part: we all, like sheep, have gone astray, and each one has turned to his own way. That's me with the recipe card RIGHT there in front of me, doing it my own way anyway.

cards.question: Everyone has gone astray like sheep. What does the LORD do with the wrong of all of them?

answers.text: He lays it all on the Servant
He leaves each one to carry it
He sends it away with the sheep

cards.text: Now watch how He takes it all: "He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth."

cards.question: The Servant stays silent while He is oppressed. Which animal is He compared to?

answers.text: A lamb led to the slaughter
A goat sent into the wilderness
A ram caught in a thicket

cards.text: As a sheep before her shearers is silent, He stays quiet. By oppression and judgment He was taken away, cut off from the land of the living.

cards.question: The Servant is cut off from the land of the living. True or false: He was stricken for His own transgression.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then comes His grave. He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in His death.

cards.question: The Servant was given a grave with the wicked. What do we learn about how He lived?

answers.text: He did no violence and told no lies
He fought back against His enemies
He hid the truth to stay safe

cards.text: Then comes a heavy line: "Yet it was the LORD’s will to crush Him and to cause Him to suffer…"

cards.question: True or false: when His soul is made a guilt offering, the Servant will prolong His days.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: He will see His offspring, and the good pleasure of the LORD will prosper in His hand. After the anguish of His soul, He will see the light of life and be satisfied.

cards.question: Now He's called My righteous Servant. What will the Servant do for many?

answers.text: Justify them and bear their iniquities
Judge them and send them away
Teach them and then leave them

cards.text: Then the prophecy says, "Therefore I will allot Him a portion with the great, and He will divide the spoils with the strong…" Strong? Friend, I lose wrestling matches to cold cookie dough.

cards.question: Why will the Servant get a portion with the great?

answers.text: He poured out His life unto death
He won a battle against the strong
He ruled over many nations

cards.text: He was numbered with the transgressors. Yet He bore the sin of many.

cards.question: The Servant was numbered with the transgressors. True or false: He made intercession for them.

answers.text: True
False
